skill.name: reducing-entropy
skill.description: Manual-only skill for minimizing total codebase size. Only activate when explicitly requested by user. Measures success by final code amount, not effort. Bias toward deletion.
skill.summary: Guides explicit deletion-first reviews that minimize final codebase size.
skill.author: softaworks

content.value_statement: Codebases grow because each change often adds more structure than it removes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a deletion-first review method for smaller final designs.
actual_capabilities: Requires loading at least one reference mindset before starting a simplification review.
Frames every change around the smallest final codebase that solves the need.
Compares before and after code size instead of implementation effort.
Identifies deletion opportunities created by a proposed change.
Lists red flags for flexibility, organization, and type-safety arguments that add code.
Documents when framework, compliance, or already minimal systems limit deletion-first reasoning.
limitations: It is manual-only and should run only when explicitly requested.
It does not calculate metrics unless the agent or user provides code context.
It can reject useful additions if maintainability, compliance, or framework rules require them.
It provides judgment prompts, not an automated refactoring engine.

use_cases.title: Refactor legacy code
use_cases.description: Find wrappers, helpers, and branches that can disappear while preserving required behavior.

use_cases.title: Review feature requests
use_cases.description: Challenge whether a new feature should be built, deferred, or reduced before implementation.

use_cases.title: Clean agent proposals
use_cases.description: Check whether an AI-generated plan adds avoidable files, wrappers, or abstractions before merging.

prompt_templates.title: Review One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use reducing-entropy on this file. Load one reference mindset, then list the smallest final design and what can be deleted.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Use reducing-entropy to compare these implementation options. Choose the option with the least final code unless a listed exception applies.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor A Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply reducing-entropy to this module. Propose a refactor that removes obsolete paths, then explain any code that must stay.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use reducing-entropy to audit this architecture. Identify abstractions, files, or features that can disappear while preserving required behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a service with many wrappers around one settings object.
output: Smallest final design: one settings record plus pure validation functions.
Delete custom wrapper classes that only forward reads and writes.

output_examples.input: Compare adding feature flags now with deferring them.
output: Keep a minimal flag mechanism because retrofitting can touch many release paths.
Reject a full targeting dashboard until a concrete need exists.

output_examples.input: Assess a refactor that splits one helper into six files.
output: The refactor adds more concepts without reducing behavior.
Prefer one focused helper unless the split removes real coupling.

best_practices: Load a reference mindset that matches the decision before proposing deletions.
Measure the final codebase size, not only the size of the immediate diff.
Name each exception, such as compliance or framework convention, before keeping extra structure.
anti_patterns: Using the skill automatically on routine requests without user consent.
Deleting framework conventions or required controls only to reduce line count.
Replacing clear code with dense code that is shorter but harder to maintain.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you want an explicit deletion-first review of refactors, feature requests, or technical debt.

faq.question: Does it write code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives review prompts and decision criteria. The agent still needs project context and user approval.

faq.question: Why does it load reference mindsets?
faq.answer: The references calibrate the review toward proven simplicity principles before judging a change.

faq.question: Can it increase code in some cases?
faq.answer: Yes. It allows exceptions when adding now avoids much larger future cost or satisfies required structure.

faq.question: Is it safe for regulated projects?
faq.answer: Use it carefully. The skill states that compliance requirements can override deletion-first reasoning.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
